A log belongs to the LOCAL calendar date of its `service_date` (D-0183 A5); every vehicle of the scope counts for the costs — retired / sold ones too (history). **The company-wide tables already exist:** the schedules with their next-due date / km are `GET /maintenance-schedules` (C1), the logs are `GET /maintenance-logs` (C2) — this report is the analysis on top.

**`summary`:** `maintenance_cost` (sum of the logs that carry a cost), `logs`, `avg_cost_per_log` (over the logs that have a cost; `null`, never `0`, when none has), `cost_per_km` (maintenance cost ÷ the completed trips' distance of the same range; `null` without cost or distance) and `vehicles_serviced` (distinct vehicles with a log), each `{ value, previous, delta_abs, delta_pct }` (`previous` / deltas only with `compare` = `previous_period` | `previous_year`; `data.previous_period { from, to }` names the window), plus `samples { logs_with_cost }`. **`series`** = one point per bucket `{ bucket, logs, cost, vehicles }` (`bucket` = the local date of the bucket start). **`by_service_type`** = `{ items [{ service_type, logs, cost, avg_cost, share_pct }], other_count }` — grouped ignoring case and surrounding spaces, most cost first (ties: more logs), `top_service_types` (1–50, default 10) limits `items`; **`by_vehicle_category`** = `[{ category | null, vehicles, logs, cost, avg_cost, share_pct }]` (stored spelling); **`top_vehicles`** = `{ items [{ vehicle { id, name, plate }, logs, cost, avg_cost, share_pct }], other_count }` (`top_vehicles` 1–50, default 10). `share_pct` = the share of the range's total cost (`null` when the total is 0).

**`schedules` is point-in-time** (there is no schedule history): the computed due state of the schedules of the vehicles IN SERVICE in scope — `{ total, by_status { overdue, due_soon, ok, unknown }, by_due_window { overdue, due_0_7, due_8_30, later, unknown }, overdue_pct }`. `by_status` is the C1 status (the company's due-soon window applies; `meta.due_soon_days` / `due_soon_km`); `by_due_window` is by DATE: overdue (any limit passed), due in 0–7 days, 8–30 days, `later` (more than 30 days away — also a schedule that is due by odometer only), `unknown` (nothing computable); `overdue_pct` = overdue ÷ the schedules that have a state (`null` when none). **`fleet.vehicles_in_maintenance_now`** = vehicles in scope whose lifecycle status is `in_maintenance` right now. **Downtime days are NOT available:** the API stores only a vehicle's current lifecycle status, no status history (KNOWN_ISSUES 11.93) — a status-history table would be a migration and an owner decision.

**Parameters:** `from` / `to` (calendar dates in the company timezone; default = the last 7 local days, today included), `interval` = `day` (default) | `week` | `month` (more than **92 buckets** → 422 naming the fix), `compare`, the vehicle scope `vehicle_category`, `cost_centre`, `vehicle_id` (comma list or `vehicle_id[]`), `yard_id` (vehicles currently checked in there) — no `driver_id` (a log has no driver). More than **200000** logs in the range → 422. **Known limits:** computed in memory per request; the schedule buckets follow the vehicles' CURRENT status; the costs are the logged `cost` only.

**The compliance report (D-0191, flow 07 B7, second half) — point-in-time.** There is no `from` / `to` / `compare`: the API keeps no history of past compliance, so the report reads every expiry date as it is now. **Records** = every compliance document of the company (vehicle and driver documents) plus the licence of every driver that is not deactivated (a driver without a licence date is a `no_expiry` record). Each record is in exactly ONE of six classes against TODAY in the company timezone (`meta.timezone`, `meta.today`): `expired`, `expiring_0_7`, `expiring_8_30`, `expiring_31_60`, `valid_after_60`, `no_expiry` — the same classes as `GET /compliance-documents/counts` (C4).

`data.summary` = `{ total, expired, expiring_0_7, expiring_8_30, expiring_31_60, valid_after_60, no_expiry, expiring_within_30_days, compliance_rate_pct, by_kind { documents, licences } }` (each block has the same fields). **`compliance_rate_pct` = records that are not expired ÷ records that have an expiry date** (`no_expiry` records are not judged; `null`, never `0`, when nothing can be judged). **`by_owner_type`** = `[{ owner_type (vehicle | driver), …block }]` for the DOCUMENTS; **`by_document_type`** = `[{ document_type, …block }]` for the documents (stored spelling ignoring case / spaces, most records first). **`upcoming`** = `[{ bucket, documents, licences, total }]` — what expires from today through today + `horizon_days` (7–365, default 90) per `interval` = `week` (default) | `month` bucket (`bucket` = the local date of the bucket start; today is the first day, so the first bucket can be partial); expired and `no_expiry` records are not in it.

**`table`** = `{ items, pagination }` (`page` 1, `per_page` 20, max 100), one row per record: `{ kind (document | licence), record_id, owner { type, id, name | null }, document_type ('Driver licence' for a licence), document_number, expiry_date, days_until_expiry (negative once expired), status }`. Filters (they narrow the table and `meta.table_counts` only): `kind`, `status` (comma list or `status[]` of the six classes; unknown → 422 `The selected status is invalid.`), `documentable_type` (`vehicle` | `driver` — documents only), `document_type` (exact, case-insensitive), `search` (owner name, document type, document number); `sort_by` = `expiry_date` (default, soonest first — expired ones first; no date last) | `owner_name` | `document_type` | `kind` (+ `sort_order`; empty values last in both directions; unknown → 422 `The selected sort by is invalid.`). **Known limits:** computed in memory per request (small tables); a document whose owner no longer exists has `owner.name` `null`.

**CSV (D-0191, B7):** the table's own filters / sort (`page` / `per_page` ignored), every matching record — kind, record id, owner type / id / name, document type, document number, `expiry_date` (date only), `days_until_expiry`, `status`. Up to 50 000 rows, otherwise 422 `Narrow the filter.`

**The drivers scorecard (D-0193, flow 07 B8, first half).** `data` = `{ summary, series, table, previous_period? }`; `meta` = `{ from, to, timezone, interval, compare, generated_at, definition_version, on_time_grace_minutes, vehicle_scope, basis }`. Nothing is stored; computed per request from `trips`, `driver_incidents` and `drivers`. **Definitions = the trips report's (D-0189):** a trip belongs to the period of its `actual_start_at`, else its `planned_start_at`, and to the TRIP'S OWN driver (so `driver_id` here — like on `/fleet/analytics/trips` — is the trip's / incident's own driver, not the vehicle's current driver as on the summary / status / performance endpoints); on-time only over the COMPLETED trips that have a planned AND an actual end (`null`, never `0`, when none can be judged), within the company's grace; distance = the trips that have an actual distance. An incident belongs to the LOCAL calendar date of its `incident_date` (D-0183 A5) and to its own driver; with a vehicle scope (`vehicle_category`, `cost_centre`, `vehicle_id`, `yard_id`) only trips of those vehicles and incidents that HAVE a vehicle in the scope count.

**`summary`:** `trips_total`, `trips_completed`, `cancellation_rate_pct`, `on_time_pct` (+ `target` from `GET /fleet/settings`), `avg_delay_minutes` (signed, negative = early), `distance_km`, `incidents`, `severe_incidents`, `incidents_per_100k_km` (incidents ÷ distance × 100 000; `null` without distance), `drivers_with_trips`, `drivers_with_incidents`, each `{ value, previous, delta_abs, delta_pct }` (`previous` / deltas only with `compare` = `previous_period` | `previous_year`; `data.previous_period { from, to }` names the window), plus `drivers_listed` (rows before search / paging) and `samples { on_time }`. The summary covers EVERY driver's activity (so its trips equal `GET /fleet/analytics/trips` for the same range) and does not follow `search` / paging. **`series`** = one point per bucket `{ bucket, trips, completed, cancelled, on_time_pct, on_time_sample, incidents, severe_incidents }` (`bucket` = the local date of the bucket start; more than 92 buckets → 422).

**`table`** = `{ items, pagination }` (always paged, default 20, max 100): one row per driver `{ driver { id, name, status }, license_number, license_expiry_date, license_state (the six C4 expiry classes against today in the company timezone), trips_total, trips_completed, trips_cancelled, trips_in_progress, trips_planned, cancellation_rate_pct, on_time_pct, on_time_sample, avg_delay_minutes, avg_duration_minutes, distance_km, incidents, incidents_minor, incidents_moderate, incidents_severe, incidents_per_100k_km, last_incident_date }`. **Rows:** every driver that is not deactivated (`active` and `suspended`), plus deactivated (`inactive`) drivers that have trips or incidents in the period (all of them with `include_inactive=1`); with a vehicle scope only the drivers that did something in it. `search` = name / licence number; `sort_by` = `driver_name` (default order asc), `trips_total` (the default), `trips_completed`, `cancellation_rate_pct`, `distance_km`, `on_time_pct`, `avg_delay_minutes`, `incidents`, `severe_incidents`, `incidents_per_100k_km`, `last_incident_date` (default order desc; empty values last in both directions; ties by name). **Not available:** idle time and harsh-driving events (no telemetry role carries them — flow 07 D1); there is no composite "score". Range > 100 000 trips or > 200 000 incidents → 422 `Narrow the range`.

**CSV (D-0193, B8):** the table's own filters / sort (`page` / `per_page` ignored), every matching driver — id, name, status, licence number / expiry date / state, trips, completed, cancelled, cancellation rate, on-time % and sample, average delay, distance, incidents (total and per severity), incidents per 100 000 km, last incident date. Up to 50 000 rows, otherwise 422 `Narrow the filter.`

**The incidents summary (D-0193, flow 07 B8, second half).** `data` = `{ summary, series, by_severity, by_type, top_vehicles, top_drivers, previous_period? }`; `meta` = `{ from, to, timezone, interval, compare, generated_at, definition_version, vehicle_scope, basis }`. Nothing is stored; computed per request from `driver_incidents` (+ the trips' distance for the rate). An incident belongs to the LOCAL calendar date of its `incident_date` (D-0183 A5); `driver_id` = the incident's own driver; with a vehicle scope (`vehicle_category`, `cost_centre`, `vehicle_id`, `yard_id`) only incidents that HAVE a vehicle in the scope count; `severity` (`minor` | `moderate` | `severe`, repeatable) and `incident_type` (case-insensitive exact) narrow the incidents. The per-item list is `GET /incidents` (D-0179).

**`summary`:** `incidents`, `severe_incidents`, `severe_share_pct` (`null` without incidents), `incidents_per_100k_km` (incidents ÷ the distance of the trips of the same period and scope × 100 000 — distance = the trips that have an actual distance, the trips report's definition; `null` without distance; `severity` / `incident_type` do NOT change the distance), `distance_km`, `drivers_involved`, `vehicles_involved`, each `{ value, previous, delta_abs, delta_pct }` (`previous` / deltas only with `compare` = `previous_period` | `previous_year`; `data.previous_period { from, to }` names the window), plus `without_vehicle` (incidents carrying no vehicle). **`series`** = one point per bucket `{ bucket, total, minor, moderate, severe }` (per day | week | month; more than 92 buckets → 422). **`by_severity`** = the three severities always, `[{ severity, count, pct }]`. **`by_type`** = `{ total, items [{ incident_type, count, severe_incidents, pct }], other_count }` — grouped ignoring case and surrounding spaces (the first spelling seen names the group), most incidents first, `top_types` (1–50, default 10) limits `items`. **`top_vehicles`** / **`top_drivers`** = the `top` (1–50, default 10) with the most incidents (ties: more severe, then id): `{ vehicle { id, name, plate } | driver { id, name }, incidents, severe_incidents, distance_km, incidents_per_100k_km }` — the rate uses that vehicle's / driver's own distance; incidents without a vehicle are not in `top_vehicles`. Range > 100 000 trips or > 200 000 incidents → 422.

**GPS-based utilisation (D-0194, flow 07 D1 + B4).** `data` = `{ summary, series, heatmap, table, previous_period? }`; `meta` = `{ from, to, timezone, interval, compare, generated_at, definition_version, scheduled_hours_per_vehicle_per_day, data_quality, basis }`. Read from the **hourly telemetry rollup** `vehicle_hourly_stats` (one row per vehicle per UTC hour, TimescaleDB hypertable, manual migration 011), filled every 15 minutes by the `fleet-telemetry-rollup` worker job from the GPS packets (`device_positions`) — attributed to the vehicle the device was assigned to at that moment; the first run backfills the whole packet history. **It is additive: the existing dashboard / vehicle-performance utilisation (completed-trip hours) is unchanged** — this is a second, telemetry-based view. Scope filters as on `/fleet/status-summary` (`vehicle_category`, `cost_centre`, `vehicle_id`, `yard_id`, `driver_id` = the vehicle's CURRENT driver); only vehicles in service (not retired / sold) count.

**Definitions:** the time between two consecutive packets is *vouched for* only when the gap is at most that interval's **gap limit** = 2.5 × the tracker's own typical report interval (the median gap of the 12 neighbouring intervals on each side, gaps under 5 s ignored), bounded to 5 minutes – 6 hours — so a tracker reporting every minute, every 15 minutes, every hour or every 3 hours all have their time counted, one lost report is bridged, an outage is not, and a tracker re-configured to another interval adapts within about a dozen packets; a brand-new device (fewer than 3 neighbouring gaps) uses the fallback `meta.data_quality.default_gap_limit_minutes` (twice the company's position-freshness window, default 30); a tracker slower than about one report every 5 hours is beyond the 6-hour cap and reads as no-data (see `coverage_pct`) — a vouched-for interval is **moving** when the earlier packet's speed is above 2 km/h (the dashboard's own threshold), otherwise **stopped**; a sensor that sends **no speed** is judged by the displacement between its two packets (above 2 km/h implied, above the 30 m drift floor, below the 250 km/h glitch ceiling) — accurate for fast reporters, an over-estimate for slow ones. **There is no idle figure:** idle cannot be told from parked without an ignition signal (`data_quality.idle_available = false`). Distance = the straight line between consecutive vouched-for packets (an under-estimate on winding roads); a GPS jump (> 250 km/h implied) adds none, nor does stationary drift. `utilisation_pct` = moving hours ÷ (vehicles that have telemetry × `scheduled_hours_per_vehicle_per_day` × local days); `coverage_pct` = vouched-for hours ÷ (vehicles with telemetry × 24 h × local days) — how much of the time the packets can speak for; `moving_share_pct` = moving ÷ vouched-for time. Hours are UTC hours summed into local days / weeks / months, so a half-hour-offset timezone is approximate at the day edges.

**`summary`:** `distance_km`, `moving_hours`, `stopped_hours`, `utilisation_pct` (+ `target` from `GET /fleet/settings`), `coverage_pct`, `moving_share_pct`, `max_speed_kmh`, `vehicles_reporting`, `packets` — each `{ value, previous, delta_abs, delta_pct }` (`previous` / deltas only with `compare` = `previous_period` | `previous_year`; `data.previous_period { from, to }` names the window) — plus `covered_hours`. **`series`** = one point per bucket `{ bucket, distance_km, moving_hours, stopped_hours, utilisation_pct, coverage_pct, vehicles_reporting, packets }` (`interval` = `hour` (up to 168 buckets, `bucket` = the local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00`) | `day` | `week` | `month` (up to 92); the vehicle set is the range's, so buckets are comparable). **`heatmap`** = 168 cells `{ dow (1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday, local), hour (0–23, local), moving_pct (moving ÷ vouched-for time; `null` when nothing is vouched for), moving_hours, covered_hours }`.

**`table`** = `{ items, pagination }` (always paged, default 20, max 100): one row per vehicle in scope `{ vehicle { id, name, plate, category }, has_telemetry, distance_km, moving_hours, stopped_hours, moving_share_pct, coverage_pct, utilisation_pct, max_speed_kmh, packets, last_packet_at, trend (moving hours per series bucket) }`; a vehicle with no rollup rows in the range is listed with `has_telemetry: false` and nulls. `search` = name / plate; `sort_by` = `moving_hours` (default, descending) | `vehicle_name` (default ascending) | `distance_km` | `stopped_hours` | `utilisation_pct` | `coverage_pct` | `moving_share_pct` | `max_speed_kmh` | `last_packet_at` (empty values last in both directions). **`meta.data_quality`** = `{ vehicles_total, vehicles_with_telemetry, rollup_latest_hour, default_gap_limit_minutes, gap_limit_rule, moving_threshold_kmh, idle_available }` — show `rollup_latest_hour` so a user can tell how fresh the numbers are. More than 600 000 hourly rows in the range → 422.

**CSV (D-0194, B4):** the table's own filters / sort (`page` / `per_page` ignored), every matching vehicle — id, name, plate, category, `has_telemetry`, distance, moving / stopped hours, moving share, coverage, utilisation, max speed, packets, last packet time (metric; empty for a vehicle without telemetry). Up to 50 000 rows, otherwise 422 `Narrow the filter.`

Nothing has been deleted yet: the first packets are from 2026-09-24.

**Retention (D-0196):** the route's `trail` comes from the raw GPS packets, kept for **12 months** (see `GET /trips/{id}/gps-trail`); for a trip older than that the trail is empty while the planned stops and their events remain.
